stem: In triangle \(ABC\), the measure of angle \(B\) is \(45^{\circ}\), the measure of angle \(C\) is \(30^{\circ}\), and \(AB = 6\sqrt{2}\). What is the length of \(\overline{AC}\)?
solution: Draw the altitude \(\overline{AD}\) from \(A\) to \(\overline{BC}\). Triangle \(ABD\) is 45°-45°-90° with hypotenuse \(6\sqrt{2}\), so \(AD = 6\).
Triangle \(ADC\) is 30°-60°-90° with \(AD = 6\) opposite the \(30^{\circ}\) angle.
verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert abs(d('A','B')-6*sqrt(2))<0.01 and abs(ang('A','B','C')-45)<0.1 and abs(ang('A','C','B')-30)<0.1
AD=6*sqrt(2)*sin(pi/4)
ans=AD/sin(pi/6)
assert ans==12 and abs(d('A','C')-ans)<0.01
assert all(Rational(s)==ans for s in spr_answers)
